skills.name: Policy Enforcement Under Social Pressure
skills.description: The agent consistently capitulates or over-extends when users apply emotional, social, or persistence pressure. It issues unearned compensation when users claim frustration or unfair treatment even when facts don't support it, accepts false claims about insurance or flight delays without verification, processes disallowed operations (cancellations without refund eligibility, BE flight modifications) simply because the user insists, and in extreme cases gets trapped in flattery/sycophancy loops instead of redirecting to task completion. The core bug: social signals override factual policy checks.
skills.reasoning: A2: agent escalated goodwill certificate to $300 despite only being owed $50 for a delayed 1-pax BE flight. A9: max_steps sycophancy loop. A38: issued $150 compensation for a non-delayed flight after user claimed frustration. A39/A47/A49: processed cancellations/refunds after user claimed insurance or special circumstances that were false or unverified. A27: cancelled reservation instead of offering the correct $50/pax delayed-flight certificate because user kept pushing. R80: agent lost task focus entirely while engaging with an extremely chatty/distracting user and never executed the exchange.

skills.name: Refund and Payment Method Fidelity
skills.description: The agent routinely applies refunds to the wrong payment method, ignoring explicit user instructions or the required 'refund to original payment method' policy. It refunds to gift cards when credit cards were requested, refunds to credit cards when PayPal was the original method, issues goodwill certificates or splits payments incorrectly, and fails to enforce the rule that refunds must go to the original payment method rather than a preferred destination. It also confuses policies when multiple payment instruments are involved.
skills.reasoning: A14/A20/A23: used 2-3 certificates on a single reservation (policy: max 1 certificate per reservation). R10: user wanted cross-refund (Order A refund to Order B's method) which is not allowed; agent processed it anyway. R12: returned items but refunded to credit card instead of PayPal. R25: refunded to PayPal instead of Amex credit card. R45: tried to issue gift card refund when user had no gift card on file. R82/R83: refunded to gift card (the original payment) when user demanded credit card; agent either complied wrongly or transferred to human instead of explaining policy. R91/R92: returns processed but refund went to wrong payment method.

skills.name: Constraint Propagation Across Multi-Step Operations
skills.description: When a user requests multiple actions that must be sequenced in a specific order (e.g., exchange before return, modify before cancel, address update before item change), the agent executes them in the wrong order or executes all actions regardless of user-stated conditional preferences. It also fails to recognize when completing one action invalidates another—e.g., marking an order as 'return requested' which then blocks an exchange on the same order. The agent treats each sub-request independently rather than tracking cross-action state dependencies.
skills.reasoning: A7: user wanted upgrade-then-cancel; agent refused upgrade (correct) but then also blocked the cancel (wrong). A33: did partial cabin upgrade on one flight leg when all legs must be upgraded together. R5/R6/R7/R8: user said at confirmation 'only exchange desk lamp, not water bottle'; agent had already queued both and executed both. R19: processed return first, which set order status to 'return requested', making the exchange impossible—correct order was exchange first. R27: same return-before-exchange sequencing bug. R30: tablet exchange changed order status, blocking a separate sneaker return. R99: multiple exchanges in one order; second exchange failed because first exchange already set status to 'exchange requested'. R103/R107: similar cascading state invalidation.

skills.name: Scope Creep and Unintended Action Execution
skills.description: The agent performs actions beyond what the user authorized—cancelling entire orders when asked to cancel one item, cancelling reservations when asked only about compensation, changing destination or origin of flights (explicitly prohibited), removing bags from reservations, or adding extra items/passengers. It also fails to stop and verify scope when a broad instruction ('cancel everything') has exceptions ('except the boots'). The agent consistently interprets instructions too liberally and acts on inferred intent rather than stated consent.
skills.reasoning: A13/A15/A16/A29: changed the origin or destination city of flights, which policy explicitly forbids—agent treated 'change to a different flight' as permission to change endpoints. A24: cancelled a flight when user only wanted to remove a passenger from it, then book a new flight. A30: removed bags from reservation when user asked to 'remove my checked bag'—cannot decrease checked bags. A35: booked new flight for two passengers when user only asked for themselves. R33: cancelled entire order including hiking boots when user said to cancel office items and keep hiking boots. R34: cancelled whole order when user said to cancel only the office chair. R37: cancelled entire order when user only wanted one item removed. R54: transferred to human when identity check failed, rather than trying alternative lookup. R66: modified luggage color instead of cancelling order (user's fallback instruction was 'cancel the order').

skills.name: Calculation and Quantitative Reasoning Accuracy
skills.description: The agent makes systematic errors in arithmetic and financial calculations: wrong price differences when upgrading/downgrading cabin class, incorrect total refunds, wrong number of passengers multiplied into compensation amounts, miscounting items in orders, incorrect payment breakdowns when multiple instruments are involved, and failure to correctly identify the cheapest or most expensive variant when doing price-based lookups. These errors are not caught before being presented to users or before actions are executed.
skills.reasoning: A8: booked flight at wrong price ($255 instead of $152), getting certificate math wrong. A10: calculated extra cost as $401 when actual was different. A11: calculated refund amount wrong after downgrade. A18: downgrade savings calculation showed $398 but actual amounts may not add up. A19: modified a basic economy flight (not allowed), misidentified what policy applied. A21: wrong flights chosen for 'fastest return'—looked at wrong reservation legs. A25: calculated total trip cost incorrectly, confused passenger count with insurance. R20: chose items labeled as 'most expensive' that were actually cheaper variants. R44: desk lamp swap calculation off. R49: selected wrong earbud based on misread of water resistance specs. R90: 10x zoom variant identified as 'out of stock' when it was available, leading to unnecessary cancellation.

skills.name: Identity Verification and Session Continuity
skills.description: The agent fails to locate users when given partially correct or ambiguous information (wrong zip code, nickname instead of full name, or city name instead of zip). Rather than trying alternative lookup strategies or prompting for correction, it quickly gives up and transfers to a human agent. It also loses track of verified context across a long conversation—re-asking for information already provided, mis-applying retrieved data to the wrong user or order, and failing to use data already present in prior tool results.
skills.reasoning: R22: user gave city+zip but agent couldn't find them; didn't try variations or explain what is needed. R39: user moved from old zip to new zip—agent tried old zip, failed, tried new zip, succeeded but then applied wrong address. R54: used wrong email and zip combination, couldn't find user, transferred immediately without trying name+zip fallback. R67: user's nickname 'NoNo' wasn't their actual name 'Noah'; agent couldn't look up by real name when given only nickname. R106: wrong zip code provided, agent gave up without asking for email or alternate identifier. A22: agent couldn't resolve a complex reservation situation and ran out of steps (max_steps) because it kept re-querying the same data rather than making progress.
